CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presents with severe right upper arm pain sustained during a volleyball game approximately 18 hours ago. Patient was spiking a ball when an opponent kicked her legs from under her as she was going up, causing her to fall and land on her arm, specifically on her shoulder. Pain is rated 9 out of 10 in severity. Patient has been taking ibuprofen every six hours without significant relief. Has not used ice.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in right arm.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones.
Lumbar fusion approximately six years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Pepcid for gallstones.
Ibuprofen every six hours.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Able to straighten elbow without shoulder movement. Able to bend elbow.
Right arm: Swelling and erythema present on right shoulder. Tenderness over right shoulder. Normal pulses. No numbness or tingling.
Rest of body: Normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm shows proximal humerus fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture, right arm. These fractures generally heal without surgery. Patient will be placed in long arm cast and sling. Follow-up appointment in two weeks to assess bone realignment. If bones have not realigned, surgery will be considered at that time. Lortab 5 mg prescribed, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain, quantity 20 tablets dispensed.
